summary: A portfolio update (up 5.24% on the week, 32.7% YTD) centered on fully exiting Shift4 (FOUR SELL) at a 35.6% loss after disappointing guidance, Middle East conflict pressure on high-margin tax-free shopping corridors, and rising debt/interest burden ($65M quarterly interest, 3.7x net leverage) — a lesson in taking losses and redeploying into accelerating businesses. What he bought instead: more Palantir (PLTR, BUY) at $125 ahead of earnings, a gamble that paid off as the stock hit $172 (+55% on his second position); he will not chase it further. He reviews Oscar Health's quarter — beats across the board but the stock dropped on doubled H2 churn guidance (2-4% monthly from CMS eligibility sweeps) and $164M of operating earnings from prior-period reserve developments — and previews a packed earnings week: Rocket Lab (thesis hinges on Neutron timing; he expects Q1 2027 launch), CoreWeave (needs margin stabilization and no more delays, since interest payments can't wait), and Nebius (BUY/HOLD — his #1 position, which he won't trade into earnings, expecting aggressive 2027 growth and diversified data centers including Europe). He also reiterates memory names like Micron ($877, ~85% gross margins) as cheap with no cracks yet, and holds cash for pullbacks. His parting point: macro rate-cut speculation is short-term noise; long-term, great executing companies are all that matter.
title: I Just Sold Out of a Stock Completely. Here's What I Bought Instead
